name: Maximum Value
description: You are given a sequence a consisting of n integers. Find the maximum possible value of (integer remainder of a i divided by a j ), where 1 ≤ i , j ≤ n and a i ≥ a j .
input_specification: The first line contains integer n — the length of the sequence ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10 5 ). The second line contains n space-separated integers a i ( 1 ≤ a i ≤ 10 6 ).
output_specification: Print the answer to the problem.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 484B — Maximum Value [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
